'''William Sparkman Overstreet''' (born October 7, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Will Overstreet Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OverWi20.htm |access-date=2024-03-10 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was selected by the Falcons in the third round of the [[2002 NFL draft]] with the 80th overall pick out of the [[University of Tennessee]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=2002 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2002/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-18 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> where he was a captain on the 2001 Tennessee team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 18, 2001 |title=Will Overstreet: Keep the Motor Running |url=https://utsports.com/news/2001/9/18/will_overstreet_keep_the_motor_running.aspx |access-date=2024-03-10 |website=University of Tennessee Athletics |language=en}}</ref> He was a member of [[Pi Kappa Alpha]] fraternity.  He played high school football at [[Jackson Prep|Jackson (Miss.) Prep]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-06-05 |title=Jackson Prep QB picks Ole Miss amid heavy recruiting buzz |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2012/jackson-prep-qb-picks-ole-miss-amid-heavy-recruiting-buzz |access-date=2024-03-10 |website=USA Today High School Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> Prior to signing with [[Tennessee Volunteers football|the Vols]] in February 1998, ''[[The Clarion-Ledger]]''newspaper named Overstreet the 1997 Metro-Jackson Area Player of the Year and selected him as a member of their All-State team.

Overstreet retired from the NFL after continued shoulder injuries. He graduated with his [[Master of Business Administration|M.B.A.]] in Finance in December 2006.  He was the founder and CEO of a software company headquartered in Knoxville, TN, called [http://www.voicesheardmedia.net/ Voices Heard Media], Inc.

Strozier was selected by the [[Denver Broncos]] in the seventh round of the [[1987 NFL draft]].<ref name="PFR2">{{Cite web |title=1987 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1987/draft.htm |access-date=October 1, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was waived by the Broncos towards the end of preseason, but signed by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] a week later.<ref name="VC 1987.09.09">{{cite news |newspaper=The Columbian (Vancouver, WA) |title=Seattle signs tight end |date=September 9, 1987 |page=D3 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-columbian-wilbur-strozier-signs-with/148680884/ |access-date=June 4, 2024 |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref> He saw action in all 12 non-strike games for the Seahawks.<ref name="PFA">{{Cite web |url=http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=STROZWIL01 |title=Wilbur Strozier Stats |website=Pro Football Archives |access-date=June 4, 2024 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160501042810/http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=STROZWIL01 |archive-date=May 1, 2016}}</ref>

Strozier spent the 1988 offseason with the Seahawks, but again was waived late in preseason.<ref name="LAT 1988.10.13">{{cite news |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |title=Ex-Dolphin Plans No Courtesy Calls to Shula |date=October 13, 1988 |page=11B |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-los-angeles-times-wilbur-strozier-si/148681246/ |access-date=June 4, 2024 |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref> He signed with the [[San Diego Chargers]] prior to week 7, and was with them for 6 games, but was released after week 12.<ref name="SBCS 1988.11.24">{{cite news |newspaper=San Bernardino County Sun (CA) |title=Transactions: NFL: San Diego Chargers |date=November 24, 1988 |page=C15 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-san-bernardino-county-sun-wilbur-str/148681534/ |access-date=June 4, 2024 |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref>

Strozier made one final effort in the NFL, with the [[Cleveland Browns]] in 1989. He was placed on the [[injured reserve list]] near the end of preseason, and was released when healthy.<ref name="NA 1989.08.30">{{cite news |newspaper=Newark (OH) Advocate |title=Browns trim club to 60 |date=August 30, 1989 |page=13 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-newark-advocate-browns-trim-club-to/148682086/ |access-date=June 4, 2024 |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref>
